question_text: What are the laws of reflection through curved mirrors?

mark_split.label: Same plane law + the curved-mirror normal

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked physically: the two laws of reflection are local — they hold at each point of any surface (plane, curved, or rough) — and for a spherical mirror the normal at a point is the radius through that point, the line joining the point to the centre of curvature C.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Equal angles law
lines: 1) The angle of incidence equals the angle
both measured from the normal at the point
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both angles are measured from the NORMAL, not from the mirror surface.
steps.why: Both angles are defined from the normal because on a curved mirror there is no single surface direction to measure from — the normal at the point of incidence is the one well-defined reference.
common_mistakes: Measuring the angles from the mirror surface instead of from the normal.
Writing the law without saying where the angles are measured.

recall.must_convey: That the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, measured from the normal at the point of incidence.

steps.memory_tip: One equation carries the mark: ∠i = ∠r, both from the normal.

steps.label: Same plane law
lines: 2) The incident ray, the reflected ray and
the normal at the point of incidence all lie
For a curved mirror the normal at any point
is the line joining that point to the centre
of curvature C. The same two laws hold at
every point of the curved surface.

lines.text: Same two laws; the normal passes through C

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The curved-mirror content is the normal: at any point it passes through C.
steps.why: The laws of reflection are local — they act at the single point where the ray lands. So they hold for plane mirrors, curved mirrors and rough surfaces alike; only the direction of the normal changes from point to point, and on a sphere that normal is the radius through the point.
common_mistakes: Thinking curved mirrors need new laws. The same two laws apply; only the normal direction varies.
Drawing the normal perpendicular to the principal axis. The normal at a point passes through the centre of curvature C.

recall.must_convey: That the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane, and that on a curved mirror the normal at a point passes through the centre of curvature.
